speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And now I call on Minister of State Alvin Tan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: As our financial industry grows in size and complexity, MAS must continually review and enhance its regulatory powers to ensure that it can effectively supervise financial institutions (FIs), as well as investigate and punish serious misconduct in our financial sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Other key amendments in the FIMA Bill pertain to the regulation of capital markets in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These amendments empower MAS to issue directions to capital markets services licence (CMSL) holders to manage potential risks from the conduct of unregulated businesses and also to enhance MAS' supervisory powers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS investigates and enforces a wide range of violations using its powers under the laws and regulations it administers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Such violations range from breaches of business conduct requirements by regulated FIs, to insider trading, fraud or deception when dealing in securities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: First, MAS reprimanded several FIs and individuals, including AIA Financial Advisers Private Limited and two Aviva entities, for breaching requirements under the FAA in relation to remuneration of supervisors as well as adequacy of risk management.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Second, following contraventions of the SFA and its business conduct requirements by Three Arrows Capital, MAS issued nine-year prohibition orders against Three Arrows Capital's Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Chairman.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For convenience, I shall refer to this latter group of legislation as the other MAS-administered Acts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: We also need to strengthen or widen some existing powers under the SFA and FAA to ensure their effectiveness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The FIMA Bill will also facilitate the transfer of evidence between MAS and other agencies for enforcement to be more efficient and more effective.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: I shall now explain the main categories of amendments in detail.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: First, MAS is proposing to introduce in the other MAS-administered Acts the power to require persons to appear before an MAS officer for examination and statement recording for the purpose of investigations under the relevant Acts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Such powers already exist under SFA and FAA and are effective in enabling investigators to obtain information about suspected misconduct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Second, the FIMA Bill will remove the requirement in SFA and FAA for MAS to first issue orders to a suspect to produce information and show that the suspect has failed to comply with such orders before MAS can enter, without a warrant, premises believed to be occupied by the suspect.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This will enable MAS to enter premises without tipping off the suspect and, therefore, reduce the risk of the suspect destroying evidence related to the investigation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: A similar power to enter premises without a warrant will be extended to the other MAS-administered Acts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: They can, however, require any person on the premises to produce information or state where such information can be found.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS officers can also require any person on the premises to preserve evidence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The FIMA Bill will also introduce provisions in the other MAS-administered Acts to empower MAS to obtain a Court warrant to search premises and seize evidence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This power already exists in SFA, FAA and TCA and it allows MAS to obtain evidence that is in the possession of uncooperative subjects before it is concealed, removed, tampered with or destroyed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The FIMA Bill will also amend the current transfer of evidence provisions in SFA and FAA to facilitate the exchange of information between MAS and the Police, Public Prosecutor or other law enforcement agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In cases where MAS investigations reveal serious misconduct that warrants a criminal prosecution, the ability for MAS to transfer evidence to the Police would be helpful.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: It reduces the need to duplicate investigations and enhances the efficiency of our law enforcement agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Conversely, there may be cases investigated by the Police or other law enforcement agencies that may be more effective or appropriately dealt with by MAS through regulatory actions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: However, under the current SFA and FAA, MAS may only transfer evidence to the Police or Public Prosecutor for the purpose of criminal investigations or proceedings for marked misconduct offences under the SFA and offences under the FAA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The FIMA Bill will expand the existing provisions to allow evidence gathered by MAS to be transferred to the Police or the Public Prosecutor for the purpose of criminal investigations or proceedings for any offence under the MAS-administered Acts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Presently, the Police or other law enforcement agencies may only transfer evidence to MAS for the purpose of civil penalty investigations or actions for market misconduct offences under the SFA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In this regard, the specific provisions for the transfer of evidence between MAS, the Police and other law enforcement agencies are consistent with the existing general common law principle permitting enforcement agencies to share with other enforcement agencies – evidence that would ordinarily be kept confidential where it is in the public interest to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Expressly legislating for the transfer of evidence between MAS, the Police and other law enforcement agencies, notwithstanding the common law principle, will make clear when evidence may be transferred and facilitate operational arrangements in respect of the transfer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This pertains to amendments specific to three Acts, namely, the SFA, the FAA and the TCA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The first set of amendments relates to expanding MAS' powers to issue directions to CMSL holders and their representatives for their unregulated businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Currently, CMSL holders may conduct unregulated businesses, such as dealing in products that are not regulated by MAS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Examples of such products include digital payment token derivatives that are traded on overseas exchanges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These unregulated businesses may pose contagion risks to CMSL holders' regulated businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For instance, losses from a CMSL holder's unregulated business could adversely impact its ability to meet its obligations to customers in its regulated businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Customers may also not be fully aware that regulatory protections do not apply to the CMSL holder's unregulated businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: While MAS has issued guidance to CMSL holders on risk-mitigating measures and safeguards that they should adopt when they conduct unregulated businesses, we should put these on a clear legal footing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: They will harmonise requirements across the Acts and where relevant, also align MAS' powers under these Acts with the Banking Act 1970.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The first relates to the appointment and removal of key persons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Regulated FIs are generally required to obtain MAS' approval before appointing their chief executive officers and directors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: However, this requirement currently does not apply to locally incorporated recognised market operators and recognised clearing houses, and approved trustees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The FIMA Bill will therefore introduce approval requirements for such entities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In addition, while MAS already has powers across the SFA, FAA and TCA to remove a director or key management officer, there are some minor differences in the grounds for removal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The FIMA Bill will consolidate the grounds for removal into a single ground of not being "fit and proper".

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Certain factors that MAS may consider, in its assessment, are also set out in the Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The second area relates to persons obtaining control of a capital markets FI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In general, a person acquiring control in capital markets FIs, must obtain MAS' approval before doing so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: However, this requirement does not currently apply to locally incorporated recognised market operators and recognised clearing houses and approved trustees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The FIMA Bill will extend the approval requirement to such entities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For other capital markets FIs, the FIMA Bill will also clarify when MAS' approval must be sought.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Currently, a person must seek MAS' approval prior to entering into an arrangement by which the person would obtain control of a CMSL holder or a licensed financial adviser.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Such an arrangement may include early stages of negotiations for the acquisition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The FIMA Bill will make clear that MAS' approval need only be sought before a person obtains control of the regulated entity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The last aspect relates to the appointment of external auditors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Presently, MAS' powers in relation to external auditors of Approved Exchanges, Approved Clearing Houses, Approved Holding Companies and Licensed Trade Repositories are limited to matters that the auditor must immediately report to the MAS, such as when the auditor becomes aware of any matter that constitutes a breach of the SFA or an offence involving fraud or dishonesty.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: It is important that the auditors appointed by such entities can satisfactorily discharge their duties, given the central role that these entities play in the capital markets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS will also have powers to direct these entities to remove or replace their appointed auditors, where the appointed auditors are unable to discharge their duties satisfactorily.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: With these amendments, MAS will align the approach for capital markets FIs with the approach that MAS has taken for other systemically important FIs under its purview, such as banks and insurance companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Lastly, the FIMA Bill will also introduce various miscellaneous amendments, such as (a) the amendments to clarify MAS' reprimand powers; (b) amendments consequential from the introduction of new processes, such as updating some of the Acts to remove references to physical licences; and (c) amendments to provide for definitions necessitated by amendments made by this Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This will further strengthen Singapore's position as a safe and trusted international financial centre.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While it is far-reaching, it aligns with our commitment to uphold the highest standards of financial supervision.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, I would like to highlight five key areas that require clarification based on feedback received by the industry.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This includes: first, clarifying the scope of MAS' powers; second, the appointment of agents by foreign regulators; third, managing risk profiles of CMSL holders; fourth, the extension of MAS' authority over the appointment and removal of key personnel; and fifth, the definition of "reasonable care on accuracy".

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The feedback has been a palpable sense of concern.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We must acknowledge and address these concerns proactively and explain the need for these powers and explain why MAS cannot simply apply for a warrant to enter.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: How do we justify these measures and are they similar in other jurisdictions, such as Australia and the United Kingdom (UK)?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Additionally, what safeguards will be put in place to prevent misuse?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In light of this, how can we ensure that entering premises and conducting interviews without a warrant will indeed enhance effectiveness in combating illicit activities?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Will this mean that agents appointed by foreign regulars can conduct inspections without a warrant as well?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Is there a reciprocal arrangement with these foreign regulators?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: How would this impact our jurisdiction's autonomy and would MAS be obliged to approve all such appointments?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Thirdly, the Bill allows MAS to issue directions on risk mitigation for unregulated business activities for CMSL holders.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Given the varied nature and scope of activities these institutions undertake, a one-size-fits-all approach could potentially overlook individual complexities.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: How will this approach ensure that unique risk profiles of these institutions are adequately managed?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Is there a plan to engage with the industry for transparent and fair standards implementation?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The extension of MAS' authority over the appointment and removal of key personnel, such as CEOs and directors, needs to be carefully managed.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The industry seeks clarity on the criteria and processes that will guide these decisions.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What are the policies in place to prevent potential overreach?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Furthermore, what is the usual timeframe for approval and how does the timeframe compare to other jurisdictions?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Understanding the criteria that will guide these significant decisions will be crucial for maintaining industry confidence.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: How will MAS assess and enforce these standards to ensure fair treatment across the board?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Furthermore, what avenues will be available for individuals to demonstrate compliance?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, the measures within it must be implemented with precision and in consultation with the stakeholders they affect.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Certainly, financial institutions will compare the new measures with those implemented in other global financial hubs.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Hence, to ensure our competitiveness as a financial centre remains robust, it is critical that we thoroughly explain the rationale behind this amendment Bill and work to convince the industry that these changes will ultimately prove advantageous for legitimate institutions operating within Singapore's jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: I would also like to declare my interest as a member of the Advisory Council of the Singapore FinTech Association.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Also, the move towards digitisation and electronic service adoption can reduce paperwork and make compliance processes more efficient.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This will encourage businesses to uphold the highest standards of compliance, enhancing our reputation for integrity and reliability in the market.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: However, this Bill will introduce several challenges that businesses may face.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: One key challenge is the increased compliance costs due to stricter licensing and regulatory requirements, which could strain the financial and operational resources of SMEs in the sector.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Additionally, the enhanced investigative powers granted to regulatory authorities may lead to a more rigorous scrutiny of business practices, requiring companies to invest more in compliance and risk management systems.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The shift towards digitisation, while beneficial in the long run, may pose short-term challenges for businesses lacking the infrastructure or expertise to adapt quickly.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, the broader regulatory scope of these amendments means that more businesses, including those involved in emerging financial products and services, will come under greater regulatory oversight, perhaps necessitating adjustments to their business models to ensure compliance.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: What would be the guidelines for the MAS to manage regulated institutions in the development of unregulated financial products?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Minister of State also please outline how SMEs will be supported in understanding and complying with new regulations, including potential briefings, training and financial assistance, while fostering confidence in the regulatory landscape?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, given the unique challenges posed by cloud services, may I clarify how MAS intends to handle investigations involving digital data stored in cloud environments, including the practicality of seizing physical evidence and ensuring the security and confidentiality of unrelated data?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Given that the financial sector is one of the pillars of our economy, this stronger regulatory oversight is paramount as the governance of financial institutions becomes increasingly important.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: In my view, these legislative amendments reflect MAS' recognition of the rapid evolution within the fintech sector and the need for a more comprehensive regulatory framework.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: These amendments will allow MAS to further develop a secure and vibrant ecosystem for fintech innovation, while ensuring the new regulatory measures are proportionate to the risks posed.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This Bill will enhance Singapore's stature as a well-regulated, leading global financial hub.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This legislative effort suggests a comprehensive approach to strengthen MAS' regulatory framework and adapt it to the evolving landscape of financial services.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the enhanced intelligence be shared with other Government agencies, such as the Singapore Police Force and the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) seamlessly, so as to investigate and prosecute money laundering and terrorism financing cases swiftly?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How can the enhanced power allow MAS to expedite investigations into licensed payment services providers for suspected failure to comply with its obligations?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Mandarin):   In order to investigate and prosecute money laundering and terrorism financing cases, can the enhanced intelligence be shared with other Government agencies, such as the Singapore Police Force and the Attorney-General's Chambers?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How can the enhanced power allow MAS to expedite investigations into licensed payment services providers for suspected failure to comply with its obligations? : This FIMA amendment Bill will allow MAS to issue written directions on the minimum standards and safeguards that should be in place when CMSL holders and their representatives conduct unregulated businesses.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, I believe MAS deserves more authority to issue stiffer measures in this aspect as an errant service provider may use consumers' investments for its unregulated activities.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What are the grounds for removal of key personnels?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What are the attributes and factors that the single fit and proper test is looking out for?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Under what circumstances will MAS approve the appointment of external auditors or agents by foreign regulators to conduct inspection of financial institutions?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What type of information will be shared with these foreign regulators?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The FIMA Bill allows for the service of notices, orders or documents by registered post and electronic services.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Has MAS considered the relevant risk factors and what measures will be imposed?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Notwithstanding the above-mentioned clarifications, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a positive move that strengthens the integrity of our financial institutions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first clarification is on enhancement and expansion of MAS' investigative powers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister of State share how much additional workload will this entail for MAS' Enforcement Department?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister of State share how the expanded investigative powers will impact the current MAS-Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) Joint Investigation Arrangement?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister of State also share what steps will be taken to ensure that MAS' enforcement officers are prepared for the expanded scope of powers?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Police are guided by the Police General Orders (PGOs) in carrying out their investigative powers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given the expanding scope of MAS' enforcement officers' powers, can the Minister of State share what equivalent guidance there is for MAS' enforcement officers?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second point is on the right against self-incrimination.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, under section 89(2) when a person claims before making a statement disclosing information that the statement might tend to incriminate the person, that statement is not admissible against the person in criminal proceedings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister of State confirm that what this means is that such a person must still provide information that might incriminate them but may preface it with a claim that the statement might incriminate them?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will the individual be informed that they can preface their statement with a claim that the statement might incriminate them?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is because if there is no such notice, individuals who know to preface their statement might tend to be those who are aware or legally advised of their right against self-incrimination.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In contrast, those who may not know of this right may tend to be those who are less privileged, socio-economically.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister of State also clarify whether this claim must strictly be made before the individual provides their statement?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What are the implications if the individual only states in the middle of the statement that it may be incriminating?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Is such a statement still admissible in criminal proceedings?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Additionally, is there a strict format or wording that such a claim must take?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the individual will be informed about their option to make such a claim, will they be informed about how they should make such a claim?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Those with limited or no legal advice on their rights against self-incrimination should not be penalised if their statement fails to meet some strict, undisclosed standard.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third and final point is on the treatment of privileged communications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister of State clarify the rationale of this requirement?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister of State also confirm that the authorities will not approach an individual to seek production of the privileged communication?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I will first deal with some general questions and comments relating to the proposed enhancements of MAS' investigative powers.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Edward Chia highlighted the importance of explaining the rationale for and consulting the industry on these amendments.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I assure Mr Edward Chia and Members of this House that MAS did issue public consultations on the proposed amendments, in which we explained how they would enhance the effectiveness of MAS' supervision and enforcement.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS carefully considered the feedback received from industry and the public and has incorporated the feedback as appropriate in the amendments.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Louis Ng asked how amendments to MAS' investigative powers will affect the workload of MAS' Enforcement Department and the current MAS-CAD Joint Investigation Arrangement.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: He also asked how MAS will ensure that its officers are equipped to exercise the expanded investigative powers and what guidance will be given to them in this regard.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This does not necessarily lead to an increase in the volume of investigations and a higher load on MAS officers.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If there is a serious cause for investigation, MAS will take it up and commit the needed resources.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The amendments will also not affect the MAS-CAD Joint Investigation Arrangement.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This Arrangement enables MAS and CAD to jointly investigate offences under the SFA as well as the FAA.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS officers taking part in the joint investigations are gazetted as Commercial Affairs Officers and exercise criminal powers of investigation, not the investigative powers under the MAS-administered Acts.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: On Mr Louis Ng's question on training and guidance to the MAS officers, I would first highlight that the expanded powers are not new to MAS.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They already exist to a large extent, in the SFA and the FAA.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS officers are experienced in conducting investigations under these Acts and I have given a few examples of such cases in my speech.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS has internal processes and guidance, which takes into account Police procedures and practices to ensure that MAS officers exercise investigative powers lawfully and judiciously.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I now turn to the Members' questions about specific proposed provisions and powers.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Louis Ng asked several questions about the proposed provisions on self-incriminating statements.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These provisions state that when being examined by an MAS officer, a person is not excused from disclosing information on the ground that the information might tend to incriminate them.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: However, if that person claims before making a statement that the information might tend to incriminate them, then that statement is not admissible against the person in criminal proceedings.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I will refer to this as the "pre-statement claim".

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Before an MAS officer starts examining a person under the MAS-administered Acts, the officer will indeed inform that person that where they claim that a statement may incriminate them, that statement would not be admissible as evidence in criminal proceedings against them.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There is no strict format or wording for the person to make a pre-statement claim.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Thus, those who are not legally represented will not be disadvantaged in terms of their ability to make such a claim.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The pre-statement claim may be made at any point during MAS' examination of the person and the information which the person claims is self-incriminating, would then be inadmissible in criminal proceedings.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS would, however, still be able to use such information to take non-criminal actions, such as civil penalties and prohibition orders.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked: one, for the rationale for requiring a legal counsel who refuses to disclose privileged communications to MAS, to provide MAS with the name and address of the person to whom the privileged communications were made; and two, if MAS will approach the person identified by legal counsel and compel the person to produce the privileged communication to MAS.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These provisions relate to situations where legally privileged communications, made by or to a lawyer, may be relevant to MAS' investigations.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The lawyer would not be required to disclose the privileged communications itself.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: However, the name and address of the person who received or made the privileged communication is not legally privileged information.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Requiring the lawyer to disclose these details would enable MAS to contact that person, to determine if the person is willing to waive privilege and disclose the privileged communication to MAS.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Don Wee asked how MAS will synergise and harmonise the information it receives with the Suspicious Transactions Reporting Office (STRO).

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: He also asked if MAS will be able to share the evidence obtained using its enhanced investigative powers with other law enforcement agencies, such as the Singapore Police Force and the AGC, for their investigations into and prosecution of money laundering and terrorism financing offences.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As for money laundering and terrorism financing offences, these may be found in laws that are not administered under MAS’ purview, such as the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Nevertheless, as I mentioned in my speech, MAS will still be able to share evidence with the Police and AGC for the purposes of investigating and prosecuting such offences based on the general common law principle permitting enforcement agencies to share confidential information with other enforcement agencies, where it is in the public interest to do so.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Don Wee also asked if the FIMA Bill would expedite MAS’ investigations into licensed payment service providers which fail to comply with their obligations.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For instance, the amendments to MAS’ investigative powers under the PS Act will empower MAS to interview and record the statement of any person, such as employees of licensed payment service providers, for the purposes of investigations under the PS Act.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The other enhancements to MAS’ evidence gathering capabilities also increase the likelihood of MAS being able to obtain relevant evidence before it is tampered with or destroyed.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS is committed to the timely enforcement of the laws and regulations under its purview.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS must investigate matters thoroughly to ensure we are able to take robust enforcement action against non-compliant persons.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Edward Chia also raised questions concerning MAS’ proposed power to enter premises without a warrant.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: He asked why MAS cannot simply apply for a court warrant to enter, if the proposed power can be found in other jurisdictions, and what safeguards will be put in place to prevent misuse.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS recognises that the ability to enter premises is a significant power.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: However, this power is necessary to enable MAS to effectively investigate potential breaches under the MAS-administered Acts.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Evidence crucial to our investigations is often found in premises occupied by a suspect.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: While legitimate financial institutions may cooperate and produce that evidence to MAS, there will be instances where the suspect is not forthcoming and there is a risk that evidence will be destroyed or concealed.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In such instances, we will require a more robust approach.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It is not necessary for the Court to act as a gatekeeper in every case where MAS wishes to exercise such powers.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There are safeguards built into the provisions themselves.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Furthermore, after entering the premises without a warrant, MAS will not be able to seize evidence without a warrant.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If MAS wishes to seize evidence, it will have to apply to the Court for a warrant to enter premises and, at the same time, seize evidence.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Chia thus asked whether the power to enter premises without a warrant will indeed be effective.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The answer to this is that it depends on the circumstances.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will assess if gaining entry without a warrant will likely result in cooperation in producing the relevant evidence.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If the assessment is that cooperation will not be forthcoming, then MAS may choose to apply for the court warrant to enter premises and seize evidence instead.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The power to enter premises without a warrant is not unique to the MAS.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Financial regulators in the UK, Australia and Canada have the power in certain situations as well.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, the UK Financial Conduct Authority has similar powers when carrying out anti-money laundering investigations.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Ontario Securities Commission can enter business premises without a warrant in respect of an investigation relating to the administration of Ontario securities laws or regulation of the capital markets in Ontario.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Each jurisdiction has its own unique regulatory frameworks and operating environment, so such considerations do inform but they do not dictate our own approach.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The underlying concern Mr Chia raised is that MAS’ power to enter premises without a warrant should not adversely affect Singapore’s competitiveness as a financial hub.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It already exists under the SFA and the FAA.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The financial industry would therefore already be familiar with MAS’ ability to enter premises in investigations in that context.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The proposed amendments will allow MAS to exercise this power to pursue misconduct more effectively and across additional sectors of the financial industry.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Neil Parekh asked how MAS intends to handle investigations involving digital data stored in cloud environments, including ensuring the security and confidentiality of unrelated data.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will also have the power to apply to the court for a warrant to search and make a copy of any digital data.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS has in place procedures and guidelines to ensure that all data obtained in the course of investigations is kept confidential.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Indeed, MAS officers have the obligation to keep such information confidential under the Official Secrets Act, the Monetary Authority of Singapore Act and prevailing Government policies.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I will now move on to the questions relating to the enhancements of MAS’ supervisory powers in the capital markets.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: On the proposed power for MAS to issue directions to CMSL holders and their representatives that conduct unregulated businesses, Mr Chia asked how MAS would exercise the new direction-making power to address and manage the unique risk profiles of each CMSL holder, given the varied nature and scope of activities that these CMSL holders undertake.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS is prepared to do the latter when there are unique risks characteristics exhibited by individual CMSL holders’ business models.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Parekh and Mr Chia also asked about MAS’ process for developing and implementing the new scope of power and standards.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Where relevant, MAS will engage the industry to keep them updated on new regulations.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Both Mr Don Wee and Mr Edward Chia have sought clarification on the criteria and processes that will guide MAS’ decision to approve the appointment of key persons or to direct their removal.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The fitness and propriety of a key person is an important consideration when MAS reviews whether to approve the appointment or direct the removal of a key person.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Wee asked about the attributes and factors MAS is looking for under the single fit and proper test, under the various Acts administered by MAS.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS may consider, for example, whether the individual has previously been convicted for fraudulent or dishonest offences.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Other factors that MAS may consider include honesty, integrity, competence and also financial soundness.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These factors and how they are assessed are also currently set out in MAS’ Guidelines on Fit and Proper Criteria.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS' guidelines therefore also make clear that an individual who does not meet any particular criteria is not automatically deemed as being not fit and proper.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS adopts a proportionate approach which considers the nature and the responsibilities of the individual in determining the relative emphasis and the standard expected of that person.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Further, the financial institution and the affected key person can appeal MAS' decision.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, if a key person is removed from office, both the affected financial institution and the key person may appeal to the Minister-in-charge.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Edward Chia also asked about the timeframe for approval of appointment of key persons.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will endeavour to make the decision in a timely manner.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: However, the time taken to process an application would depend on factors such as the complexity of the application, the completeness of the information and documents provided, and any additional clarification that might be required.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Wee and Mr Chia raised a few questions on the proposal to empower MAS to approve appointment of agents by foreign regulators to conduct inspections of financial institutions on their behalf.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will approve such appointments when it is satisfied that the inspection of the financial institution is relevant to the foreign regulator’s discharge of its regulatory function and mandate.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: An example would be where the MAS-regulated financial institution is part of a financial services group under the consolidated supervision of the foreign regulator.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS similarly conducts onsite inspections of regulated financial institutions in foreign jurisdictions under comparable arrangements.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These are inspections which rely on the cooperation of the financial institution and are not investigations and the question of a warrant does not arise.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Edward Chia also asked about the type of information that will be shared with such foreign regulators.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These would generally include compliance policies and procedures of the inspected financial institution as well as transaction information that may be relevant to the scope of the inspection.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In granting its approval, MAS has the power to impose conditions or restrictions to ensure that the appropriate safeguards are in place, such as those for the protection of confidentiality of information.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Don Wee asked whether MAS has considered the relevant risk factors for the service of notices, orders or documents, or the "relevant documents", by registered post and electronic service, and what measures will be imposed.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If served through registered post, the envelope containing the relevant documents should be properly addressed, stamped and posted by registered post.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Edward Chia sought clarification on what constitutes exercising "reasonable care" in the submission of information to MAS.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is the same standard of care that is already adopted for the existing offences for the provision of false or misleading material information under the SFA, FAA and TCA.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS is simply extending this standard of care to the provision of non-material false or misleading information.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This new offence does not apply to individuals.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Chia also asked how MAS will assess and enforce proposed standards to ensure fair treatment across the board.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It is not MAS' intent to automatically or mechanistically take financial institutions to task for errors in their submissions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Are there any clarifications for Minister of State Tan?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.40 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 3.17 pm until 3.40 pm.
